arxiv-2210-05869.title: Quantum Chaos in the Extended Dicke Model
arxiv-2210-05869.creator: Qian Wang
arxiv-2210-05869.description: Abstract We systematically study the chaotic signatures in a quantum many-body system consisting of an ensemble of interacting two-level atoms coupled to a single-mode bosonic field, the so-called extended Dicke model. The presence of the atom-atom interaction also leads us to explore how the atomic interaction affects the chaotic characters of the model.

arxiv-2212-01456.title: A Standardized Framework for Collecting Graduate Student Input in Faculty Searches Python ( Van Rossum & Drake 2009 )
arxiv-2212-01456.creator: Yasmeen Asali, Konstantin Gerbig, Aritra Ghosh, Christopher Lindsay, Zili Shen, Marla Geha
arxiv-2212-01456.description: Abstract We present a procedure designed to standardize input received during faculty searches with the goal of amplifying student voices. The framework was originally used to collect feedback from graduate students, but it can be adapted easily to collect feedback from undergraduate students, faculty, staff or other stakeholders.

arxiv-2401-14777.title: Large Language Model Adaptation for Financial Sentiment Analysis
arxiv-2401-14777.creator: Pau Rodriguez Inserte, Mariam Nakhlé, Raheel Qader, Gaëtan Caillaut, Jingshu Liu
arxiv-2401-14777.description: Abstract Natural language processing (NLP) has recently gained relevance within financial institutions by providing highly valuable insights into companies and markets’ financial documents. However, the landscape of the financial domain presents extra challenges for NLP, due to the complexity of the texts and the use of specific terminology.

arxiv-2403-14076.title: Improving Λ \Lambda Signal Extraction with Domain Adaptation via Normalizing Flows
arxiv-2403-14076.creator: Anselm Vossen
arxiv-2403-14076.description: Abstract The present study presents a novel application for normalizing flows for domain adaptation. The study investigates the ability of flow based neural networks to improve signal extraction of Λ \Lambda Hyperons at CLAS12. Normalizing Flows can help model complex probability density functions that describe physics processes, enabling uses such as event generation.

arxiv-2503-03983.title: Audio Flamingo 2: An Audio-Language Model with Long-Audio Understanding and Expert Reasoning Abilities
arxiv-2503-03983.creator: Sreyan Ghosh, Zhifeng Kong, Sonal Kumar, S Sakshi, Jaehyeon Kim, Wei Ping, Rafael Valle, Dinesh Manocha, Bryan Catanzaro
arxiv-2503-03983.description: Abstract Understanding and reasoning over non-speech sounds and music are crucial for both humans and AI agents to interact effectively with their environments. In this paper, we introduce Audio Flamingo 2 (AF2), an Audio-Language Model (ALM) with advanced audio understanding and reasoning capabilities.

arxiv-2503-06579.title: An agent-based model of citation behavior
arxiv-2503-06579.creator: George Chacko, Minhyuk Park, Vikram Ramavarapu, Ananth Grama, Pablo Robles Granda, Tandy Warnow
arxiv-2503-06579.description: Abstract Whether citations can be objectively and reliably used to measure productivity and scientific quality of articles and researchers can, and should, be vigorously questioned. However, citations are widely used to estimate the productivity of researchers and institutions, effectively creating a ‘grubby’ motivation to be well-cited.

arxiv-2512-07545.title: On the Asymptotic Evolution of Bulk-viscous, Spherically Symmetric Spacetimes
arxiv-2512-07545.creator: Balázs Endre Szigeti, Imre Ferenc Barna, Gergely Gábor Barnaföldi
arxiv-2512-07545.description: Abstract The scale-free nature of gravitational interaction in both Newtonian gravity and the general theory of relativity gives rise to the concept of self-similarity, where solutions are scale invariant. As a result of this property, the governing partial differential equations are greatly simplified and can be transformed into ordinary ones.

arxiv-2512-10563.title: NormCode: A Semi-Formal Language for Auditable AI Planning
arxiv-2512-10563.creator: Xin Guan, Yunshan Li, Zekun Wu, Ruibo Zhang
arxiv-2512-10563.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xin Guan, Yunshan Li, Zekun Wu, Ruibo Zhang. As AI systems move into high-stakes domains—legal reasoning, medical diagnosis, financial decision-making—regulators and practitioners demand auditability: the ability to trace exactly what each step in a multi-step workflow saw and did. Yet current LLM-based workflows are fundamentally opaque. Context pollution —the accumulation of information across reasoning steps—causes models to hallucinate and lose track of constraints, while implicit data flow makes it impossible to reconstruct what any given step actually received.

pmc-10738876.title: NEIGHBORHOOD DISADVANTAGE, IMAGING BIOMARKERS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, AND COGNITION IN DIVERSE OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10738876.creator: Erica Fan, Sarah Royse, Beth Snitz, Tharick Pascoal, C Shaaban, Brian Lopresti, Victor Villemagne, Ann Cohen
pmc-10738876.description: Neuroimaging biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are well-validated in White populations. However, it remains unclear how these biomarkers are associated with cognition in non-White populations disproportionately affected by systemic socioeconomic discrimination. We investigated whether neighborhood disadvantage modifies associations of neuroimaging biomarkers with cognition in a diverse cohort of 198 adults ≥50 years, 50% of whom are Black.

pmc-11303123.title: Multiomics analysis of canine myocardium after circumferential pulmonary vein ablation: Effect of neuropeptide Y on long‐term reinduction of atrial fibrillation
pmc-11303123.creator: Qiyuan Song, Ning Zhang, Yujiao Zhang, An Zhang, Huilin Li, Shuting Bai, Luxiang Shang, Juanjuan Du, Yinglong Hou
pmc-11303123.description: Catheter ablation (CA) is an essential method for the interventional treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF), and it is very important to reduce long‐term recurrence after CA. The mechanism of recurrence after CA is still unclear. We established a long‐term model of beagle canines after circumferential pulmonary vein ablation (CPVA).

pmc-11380650.title: Feasibility and Safety of Early Oral Feeding After Radical Gastrectomy in Patients With Gastric Carcinoma: A Systematic Review
pmc-11380650.creator: Wahida Ali, Wahidullah Dost, Mohammad Nazir Zaman, Mohammad Qaher Rasully, Jamaluddin Niazi, Farzad Qasemi, Raisa Dost, Wahida Dost, Danyal Bakht, Syed Faqeer Hussain Bokhari
pmc-11380650.description: This systematic review examines the feasibility and safety of early oral feeding (EOF) after radical gastrectomy in patients with gastric cancer. A comprehensive literature search identified eight eligible studies, including both clinical trials and cohort studies, conducted between 2011 and 2020.

pmc-11450126.title: High Fe-Loading Single-Atom Catalyst Boosts ROS Production by Density Effect for Efficient Antibacterial Therapy
pmc-11450126.creator: Si Chen, Fang Huang, Lijie Mao, Zhimin Zhang, Han Lin, Qixin Yan, Xiangyu Lu, Jianlin Shi
pmc-11450126.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Highlights Fe single-atom catalysts (h3-FNCs) with high loading, high catalytic activity and high stability were synthesized via a method capable of increasing both the metal loading and mass-specific activity by exchanging zinc with iron.The “density effect,” derived from the sufficiently high density of active sites, has been discovered for the first time, leading to a significant alteration in the intrinsic activity of single-atom metal sites.The superior oxidase-like catalytic performance of h3-FNCs ensures highly effective bacterial eradication.

pmc-11709147.title: Regulation of autophagy by protein lipidation
pmc-11709147.creator: Yuqian Shao, Junchao Hu, Huihui Li, Kefeng Lu
pmc-11709147.description: Autophagy is a conserved catabolic recycling pathway that can eliminate cytosolic materials to maintain homeostasis and organelle functions. Many studies over the past few decades have demonstrated that abnormal autophagy is associated with a variety of diseases. Protein lipidation plays an important role in the regulation of autophagy by affecting protein trafficking, localization, stability, interactions and signal transduction.

pmc-13092650.title: Functionalized Quantum Dot‐Based Portable Sensor for Dual Detection of Stress Biomarkers in Blood Serum and Saliva
pmc-13092650.creator: Anusha Kishore, Arun Mathew Varughese, Bernhard Roth, Carsten Zeilinger
pmc-13092650.description: This work reports on the simultaneous detection of cellular stress biomarkers in blood and saliva, using a portable sensor. We expanded the application of our optical measurement system, the Transilluminated Quantum Dot (TIQD) imager, paired with a low‐cost biochip for minimally invasive biomolecule detection.
